title: The Present Indicative of Strong Verbs
subtitle: Rīdan (to ride) — Class I ablaut.
objectives: Understand and apply the concepts of The Present Indicative of Strong Verbs.
Read and parse examples from authentic Old English texts.

sections.heading: Core concept
sections.body: Strong verbs form their past tense by changing the root vowel (ablaut), not by adding a dental suffix. Old English has seven classes of strong verbs, each with a different ablaut pattern. Class I: ī - ā - i - i. Present: ic rīde, þū rītst / rīdest, hē rītt / rīdeþ, wē / gē / hīe rīdaþ.

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: Ic rīde (I ride), þū rītst (you ride), hē rītt (he rides), wē rīdaþ (we ride).
